keyFindings.text: "User need" has no dedicated authored field at Levels 1-2. The only `As a … I want … so that …` surface is `## 11. USER STORIES`, emitted inside an `<!-- IF level:3,3+ -->` block [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/spec.md.tmpl:326-347]. At Levels 1-2 the user need exists only as prose inside the Problem Statement, so nothing structural distinguishes it from the problem description.

`goal.md` is the only surface with a durable one-line statement of intent: `## 1. DURABLE DIRECTIVE` / `**Objective:** [One sentence. What this packet is for…]`, and its anchors are required whenever the document exists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl:38-41; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts:242-246]. It is a lazy addon, so a packet that did not ask for it has no durable directive at all [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:levels.1.lazyAddonDocs].

Every authored spec level writes the problem and purpose exactly once, in one section: `## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE` with `### Problem Statement` and `### Purpose`. The core template carries it for Levels 1-3 and 3+ [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/spec.md.tmpl:99-107]; the phase-parent template carries the same two subsections [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:63-72]; the research-record template carries it too [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/research.spec.md.tmpl:57-67].

No validation rule reads the purpose prose. Grep counts for `problem` are zero across the validator modules (measured this iteration), and the only content-shaped checks are placeholder tokens (`PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`) and the non-empty-anchor-body check, which fires only when an anchor is present and empty [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:752-756, 889-899; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts:1193-1200]. A spec that keeps the section and writes a vacuous sentence passes.

Required-section enforcement exists but is gated on the template stamp. `ANCHORS_VALID` requires every anchor whose template section is a required H2, but only for documents carrying a `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE … v2.3` or newer stamp [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:758-768, 1028-1035]. A v2.4 `spec.md` that deletes the whole `PROBLEM & PURPOSE` section fails with a named missing anchor; an older, unstamped document keeps only the integrity check.

The level contract requires only mechanical docs. Levels 1-3 require `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`; `implementation-summary.md` becomes required only after implementation starts; `handover.md`, `goal.md`, `timeline.md`, `decision-record.md` and `research/research.md` are `lazyAddonDocs` (scaffolded only on request), and `acceptance-criteria.md` is an optional addon at Levels 2-3, required only through the separate `AC_CLOSURE` rule [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:levels.1.requiredCoreDocs/lazyAddonDocs/optionalAddonDocs; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/structure/folder-structure.md:158-190].

The phase level requires `spec.md` alone, and its section-gate table declares `problem` as required for `spec.md` at `phase` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:levels.phase.requiredCoreDocs; levels.phase.sectionGates["spec.md"].problem]. So the declared contract does name the purpose section as required at parent level.

The phase parent is explicitly exempt from that check, so the parent's declared `problem` requirement is not executed. `ANCHORS_VALID` returns early for a folder classified as a phase parent with `'Phase parent lean document set accepted'` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:963-970]. The other sufficiency loop enforces missing anchors only for `timeline.md` and `goal.md` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts:1182-1191]. Net effect: a phase parent's `spec.md` can lose Problem & Purpose entirely and still validate.

The two successor-facing surfaces carry no purpose field. `handover.md` has sections Handover Summary, Context Transfer, For Next Session, Validation Checklist, Session Notes and no problem/purpose heading [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/handover.md.tmpl:37,50,84,107,121]; the `_memory.continuity` block carries `recent_action`, `next_safe_action`, `blockers`, `key_files`, `completion_pct`, `open_questions`, `answered_questions` and no purpose or problem key [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/implementation-summary.md.tmpl:38-63]. `acceptance-criteria.md` likewise has no purpose column: `AC-ID`, `REQ`, `Given / When / Then`, `Verification`, `Status`, `Waiver` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl:57-66].

`/speckit:handoff` saves continuity before writing the note and hands the receiving session to `/speckit:resume` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/handoff.md:42,61,78-88], and the handover template has no purpose heading [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/handover.md.tmpl:37,50,84,107,121]. Even an author who adds a purpose paragraph has no reader: the handover parser looks only for four labelled fields, so the paragraph can travel only accidentally through `collectSummaryLines` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:632-640,405-417].

`/speckit:resume` parses each tier into a fixed signal shape that has no purpose field: `summary`, `recentAction`, `nextSafeAction`, `blockers`, `keyFiles`, `documents`, plus an optional `packetPointer` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:56-72]. The handover tier reads only the labelled values `Recent action`, `Next safe action`, `Blockers`, `Key files` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:632-673]; the continuity tier maps the thin record's six fields into the same shape [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:677-712].

`/speckit:save`'s writer contract is explicitly compact and mechanics-only: the documented payload fields are `recent_action` and `next_safe_action` (≤96 chars / ≤16 words), `blockers` and `key_files` (≤5 short items), plus the stored `completion_pct` and question lists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/continuity/generate-context.ts:170-181]. The thin record has no purpose field [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:60-78], so a purpose survives a save only as a packet document, never as continuity state.

`session-prime.ts` emits pointers, not content. At startup its fallback surface is the continuity line `- Continuity: recover on demand from the packet docs` plus `/speckit:resume — recover the active packet from its canonical docs` and the `rg` hint [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:230-258]; after a compaction it prints `Context was compacted. Run /speckit:resume against the active packet to recover session state.` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:135-170]. Recovery is delegated to the packet docs; the hook itself never states what the packet is for.

Claude's PreCompact hook reads only the live transcript tail. It extracts active file paths, recent topics, working-memory attention signals and the last five meaningful transcript lines, adds a detected `Active spec folder: <path>` line, and merges those into a token-budgeted brief [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:443-492]. It opens no packet document: spec.md, handover.md and the continuity block are never read on this path, so the packet arrives as a path string and nothing else.

Even on the continuity path the injected facets carry no purpose. `buildContinuityFacets` fills the facet labelled "Goal" from `next_safe_action`, "Decision" from answered-question ids, "Progress" from `recent_action` + summary + touched files, and "Gotcha" from blockers + open questions [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:289-303]. The renderer then prints those four headings with the literal labels `Goal`, `Decision`, `Progress`, `Gotcha` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:307-323]. So the one line a compacted session reads under the word "Goal" is the next action, which is the exact substitution the operator reported.

The deep-loop hop is the exception: the child-dispatch brief carries purpose-shaped text. `buildLoopPrompt` injects `research_topic: <full topic>` into the child prompt [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:1655-1669], and the per-iteration prompt pack renders `Research Topic: {research_topic}` plus focus and remaining questions on every iteration [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl:11-16]. A research loop therefore restates its purpose by construction; an ordinary implementation session has no equivalent field at any hop.

The hook has a continuity-aware path, but it is opt-in: `authoredSnapshotEnabled(input)` is true only when the hook input sets `authored_continuity_snapshot: true` or `continuity_snapshot: 'authored'` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:348-355]. Default compaction does not pass that flag, so the authored snapshot worker is skipped [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:608-630].

The operator-facing brief has no purpose row: `RESUME BRIEF` renders Spec, Confidence, Source, Now, Last confirmed, Next safe action, Blockers, Progress and "Why this is next" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-presentation.txt:116-129]. The restore panel that feeds it is capped at 8 items and 1,200 characters and is built from the same four facets, so a purpose string would compete with next-action and key-file items for the same budget [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:507-560].

The other runtimes split into two groups, and neither group recovers purpose. Codex's PreCompact adapter hands the event to the Claude implementation (`runClaudeHookAdapter('compact-inject.js', …)`) [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/compact-inject.ts:36-38]. DSH's compaction handler reuses the shared session-prime output as its base context and appends the same `/speckit:resume` recovery pointer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-compact-context.mjs:7,122,126-142], where that prime output is the spawned Claude session-prime hook's stdout [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-start-context.mjs:44-58]. Pi and Devin compose their own recovery sections: the retained compaction summary, `## Active Spec Folder\n<path>`, and `## Recovery\nRun /speckit:resume …` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/pi/session-compact-context.ts:141-190; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:266-290]. No hook outside Claude imports the authored-snapshot module, and no hook calls the resume ladder at all (grep over `runtime/hooks` found one importer, `claude/compact-inject.ts:40`).

The spec-docs fallback tier cannot recover purpose either. It takes the title plus the first three non-heading, non-table lines as the summary, and *synthesizes* the next action as `Review tasks.md and continue the packet.` or `Review <primary>.md and continue the packet.` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:758-790; collectSummaryLines at :405-417]. A packet's Problem & Purpose paragraph can reach the brief only by happening to sit inside those first three plain body lines — `## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE` is a heading and is filtered out.

`handover.md` does not carry a purpose field in practice. Of 97 handover files, **0** have a Purpose heading. 22 contain a purpose/problem/objective string somewhere, and inspection shows those are incidental: a checklist row that points back at `spec.md` ("Spec file: `spec.md` (root purpose and the phase map)"), a trap-table note about a "purpose-built" port, a frontmatter `description` field, and a "Related" pointer to `goal.md` [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/loop-architecture/001-deep-loop-innovation/012-runtime-enablement/handover.md:173] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/memory-search-and-knowledge/001-graph-and-context-optimization/003-memory-and-causal-runtime/003-embedder-testing-and-architecture/001-local-embeddings-foundation/handover.md:80] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/memory-search-and-knowledge/001-graph-and-context-optimization/003-memory-and-causal-runtime/001-continuity-memory-runtime/003-continuity-refactor-gates/handover.md:32].

keyFindings.text: The parent's purpose is a container purpose, and it is already stale. The 481-character statement describes the decomposition ("hold the thirty-eight packets as phases … with a timeline, literal names, and retrieval"), not a user need, and the count it states (38) no longer matches the 69 numbered children [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/runtime-and-release/001-system-speckit-v4/spec.md:71]. keyFindings.text: Candidate (a), parent-level acceptance criteria, fails the gap test and costs the most. `acceptance-criteria.md` has no purpose column (AC-ID, REQ, Given/When/Then, Verification, Status, Waiver) [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl:57-66]; the phase level declares no optional addon docs, so enabling the file at parent level needs the level manifest, the `AC_CLOSURE` rule scope, `create.sh` seeding and the template — four or more edit points [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:1848] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/rules/check-ac-closure.sh:1]. Only 10 of 319 parents carry the file today.

Candidate (b), a parent-level user story or purpose-and-problem section, is a no-op as written: the phase-parent template already has Problem & Purpose [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:63-72], and iteration 1 measured that the phase validator exempts parents rather than requiring the section [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:963-970]. Adding the section again changes no artifact and crosses no hop; it becomes useful only when a hop reads it.

Candidate (c), an improved parent-specific template, cannot close the gap on its own for the same reason: the parent template already carries the purpose and the missing piece is a reader. A user-story block could ride along in the same edit as a read-side change, but as a standalone candidate it changes authoring only.

Candidate (d), a purpose field in the continuity block, is the most expensive. It needs the thin-record interface and its `MEMORY_0NN` validation, the compact serializer, the save writer's documented payload contract, the implementation-summary template and the resume parser, plus a fallback story for the 4,657 existing `implementation-summary.md` files that have no such field [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:60-78; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/continuity/generate-context.ts:170-181]. It also leaves the 29 handover-only packets uncovered.

Candidate (e), a purpose line in the compaction brief, is feasible and cheap on Claude: the active packet is resolvable without the transcript because `lastSpecFolder` is persisted in hook state [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/hook-state.ts:345], so one extra file read supplies the purpose. It covers only the compaction hop, and pi/devin compose their own sections, so it needs per-runtime wiring [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:270-290].

Candidate (f) is also the widest coverage per unit of effort, because every runtime's recovery surface already delegates to `/speckit:resume`: Claude's compaction output tells the session to run it [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:135-170], dsh appends the same pointer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-compact-context.mjs:122,126-142], and devin and pi emit `## Recovery\nRun /speckit:resume …` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:266]. One read-side addition therefore reaches every hop the operator described, and it also fixes the misleading facet label from iteration 2 by making the real purpose available next to the next action.

Candidate (f), one purpose row on the resume surface, is the smallest change that closes the measured gap. The ladder already reads `spec.md` among its spec-doc snapshots before it chooses a primary tier [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:1128-1141], and its signal shape is one interface plus one renderer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:56-72; .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-presentation.txt:116-129]. Cost: two files and one test — add `purpose` to the signal, extract `### Purpose` from the snapshot already in memory (falling back to an author-labelled `**Objective:**` line when present, of which the corpus has one example [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/z_archive/022-sk-deep-research-evolution/005-sk-deep-research-review-mode/handover.md:33]), and render a `Purpose:` row in the RESUME BRIEF. No schema change, no migration, no new authoring.

No hop reads `goal.md`. References to `goal.md` number 0 in `resume-ladder.ts`, 0 across `runtime/hooks/**`, and 0 in `runtime/lib/continuity/**` [INFERENCE: grep counts run this iteration over those three trees]. The durable directive is an authored purpose carrier with no reader, which places the gap on the read side rather than the authoring side.

Parent-level purpose is already authored in two machine-readable carriers, and neither is the artifact the operator proposed. The phase-parent template carries `## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE` with Problem Statement and Purpose [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:63-72], and `goal.md` carries `## 1. DURABLE DIRECTIVE` with a one-sentence `**Objective:**` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl:38-41]. In the live corpus there are 319 phase parents, of which 94 carry `goal.md` and only 10 carry `acceptance-criteria.md` [INFERENCE: measured by the parent walk described in Actions Taken, this iteration].

Validation plan for the recommendation: a fixture test in `resume-ladder.vitest.ts` with a packet whose `spec.md` Purpose is filled (assert the signal carries it and the brief renders the row), a second fixture whose only carrier is `goal.md` (assert the objective is used), and a negative fixture with neither (assert the row is omitted rather than rendering "None"); then one manual `/speckit:resume` against this packet and a check that the rendered brief shows the purpose line [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/tests/resume-ladder.vitest.ts].

Correction to iteration 4's candidate (f): the cheapest closing change is not a code change in the ladder but one row in the resume workflow's reply format — `Purpose` — plus the matching instruction in the ladder step, in both the auto and confirm assets and the presentation template. That is three text assets, no schema, no migration, and the workflow already reads `spec.md` (the third rung of its ladder), so the value is on hand [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:105-112,138]. This supersedes iteration 4 finding 8's file list while keeping its read-side reasoning.

Ruled out — a parent-level user story or purpose/problem section as a standalone change: the phase-parent template already carries Problem & Purpose [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:63-72] and the phase validator exempts parents [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:963-970], so the candidate adds an artifact no hop reads.

Ruled out — a purpose field in the continuity block as the *cheapest* option: it is the most expensive (thin record + `MEMORY_0NN` validation + save payload + template + parser), needs a fallback for the 4,657 existing summaries, and leaves the 29 handover-only packets uncovered [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:60-78].
Ruled out — an improved parent-specific template as the closing change: the parent template already carries the purpose; the defect is the absence of a reader, which a template cannot supply.

Ruled out — parent-level acceptance criteria: no purpose column in the AC schema, only 10 of 319 phase parents carry the file, and enabling it at parent level touches the manifest, the `AC_CLOSURE` rule scope, `create.sh` seeding and the template [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl:57-66; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:1848].

Ruled out — relying on authors to restate the purpose in handovers: 0 of 97 handovers has a Purpose heading and exactly one restates an objective, as a bullet no parser reads [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/z_archive/022-sk-deep-research-evolution/005-sk-deep-research-review-mode/handover.md:33].

Ruled out — the compaction brief as the primary carrier: it is feasible on Claude because `lastSpecFolder` is persisted in hook state [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/hook-state.ts:345], but it covers one hop and needs per-runtime wiring, and Claude's own compaction path is opt-in for continuity [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:348-355].

Ruled out — using validation as the lever: the only executed required-anchor check exempts phase parents, and the phase level's declared `problem` gate is never executed, so a validation change would enforce authoring at the parent while leaving every hop untouched. It is a different change from the one the evidence supports, and it would not close the measured gap.

The interactive `/speckit:resume` brief is not produced by the programmatic ladder. The command workflow carries its own continuity ladder — read `handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity`, then the canonical spec docs, then a ripgrep recipe only for a named gap [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:105-112] — and its reply format fixes the visible fields at `Confidence`, `Context source`, `Now`, `Last confirmed`, `Next safe action` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:138]. `Purpose` is not among them.

The programmatic ladder has exactly one non-test consumer: `refreshAuthoredContinuitySnapshot` in `authored-continuity-snapshot.ts`, which calls `buildResumeLadder({ specFolder, workspacePath })` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/authored-continuity-snapshot.ts:201], and that module is imported only by Claude's opt-in compaction path [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:40]. A `ResumeSignal` change alone would therefore improve only the opt-in snapshot, not the brief every operator sees.
